//: THE GATEWAY'S DECLARED RELATIONSHIP TO elitea-sdk.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The /llm surface has exactly one first-class client:
elitea-sdk. Its budget reader, its two base paths and its LangChain dialects
decide what a correct gateway answer looks like. Until this file existed the
gateway declared no relationship to the SDK at all, so an SDK bump could not
fail any gateway gate. The compatibility defect that shipped survived for
that reason: the gateway put the refusal SCOPE in error.type, the SDK reads
the scope from error.code, budget_exceeded_from returned None, and a policy
refusal reached the model as message content. Every Go test agreed, because
every Go test restated the same wrong literal.
THIS FILE IS NOT A SECOND COPY OF THE PIN. The revision itself is owned by
services/elitea-worker-python/elitea-sdk.lock.json, which the worker image
and .github/workflows/ci-python.yml already build from. What the gateway
owns is the statement below: the revision against which the gateway's
compatibility gates were LAST RUN AND SEEN TO PASS.
HOW IT FAILS. internal/sdkpin/pin_test.go reads both files and compares
them. Move the SDK in the lock file and the gateway test job turns red,
with no gateway source change at all. That is the gate this file adds.
THAT CLAIM DEPENDS ON A PATH FILTER, so do not delete it. A lock-file-only
bump touches no file under services/elitea-llm-gateway/, so ci-gateway.yml
names services/elitea-worker-python/elitea-sdk.lock.json in BOTH its
pull_request and push arms. Without that line the job never starts on the
one change this gate exists to catch, and the sentence above is false.
WHY THE CONTENT DIGESTS ARE BELOW (#567). A revision names WHICH commit is
checked out. It does not name WHAT the working tree holds. Both gates ran
`git rev-parse HEAD`, compared it with the revision, and stopped. Two holes
followed. A DIRTY tree keeps the pinned HEAD, so uncommitted SDK edits stay
invisible. `git rev-parse` also walks UP to an enclosing repository, so a
hand-authored directory inside a pinned clone reports the pinned revision.
An operator whose checkout is dirty then mints a pin from a green run that
measured other bytes.
The `contents` list records the sha256 of every SDK file the two gates
read. Tier 1 and tier 2 hash those files in the checkout and REFUSE TO RUN
when a digest differs, so the gates measure the content this file names.
THE LIST IS SCOPED ON PURPOSE. ci-python.yml applies the two patch
revisions with `git cherry-pick --no-commit`, so the CI tree is
deliberately dirty. A whole-tree cleanliness check fails every CI run, and
that trap is why this states FILES instead. Both patches touch
elitea_sdk/runtime/toolkits/mcp.py, elitea_sdk/runtime/utils/mcp_adapter.py
and tests/ only, so neither digest below moves under them.
WHEN THE SDK MOVES:
1. Update services/elitea-worker-python/elitea-sdk.lock.json as usual.
2. Run tier 1:  ELITEA_SDK_SOURCE_ROOT=<new checkout>
python -m pytest scripts/contract/test_sdk_budget_contract.py
3. Run tier 2:  services/elitea-llm-gateway/scripts/sdk-conformance/run.sh
4. Read the new digests from the new checkout:
cd <new checkout> && sha256sum elitea_sdk/runtime/exceptions.py \
elitea_sdk/runtime/clients/client.py     # macOS: shasum -a 256
5. ONLY when both gates pass, copy the revision, the patch revisions and
the digests here. Copying them first turns a real incompatibility into
a green build.
ADD A FILE TO `contents` WHENEVER A GATE STARTS READING IT. Tier 1 compares
this list with the SDK files it reads and fails when they differ, so a new
gate input cannot stay unmeasured.
verified_on is a date for the reader. Nothing keys on it.
